questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: My stay abroad is mandatory on my bachelor, so naturally I thought it was exciting and would give my both academic and career opportunities.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The destination was chosen for us. I am studying Turkish, so of course it would be Turkey. And the University of Copenhagen has an agreement with the university in Ankara.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Before we even got to our destination, we were had an contact person at our host university. That was very nice. And upon arrival she helped us a lot, and gave us the information that we needed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Before we even got to our destination, we were had an contact person at our host university. That was very nice. And upon arrival she helped us a lot, and gave us the information that we needed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was so lucky that a have a friend who lives in Turkey. He was very helpful, and he helped us find somewhere to live. It was a bit difficult to find someone who would want to rent their apartment for "only" 5 month. I would recommend, maybe to stay on campus when you arrive and then by yourself, try to find somewhere to live off campus close to the city. I would reeeeally recommend living in the city and not outside.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is of course more expensive. There is also the cost of public transport. I would recommend to live as close to the big city as possible, it's nicer and there is more to do.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: When we arrived we were told to go to the "Student Affairs Office". It is located on campus. They just needed our passport and then they could register us in the system. We then needed to make a student ID card, we got some papers and we gave them to another office, also located on campus. And then 3 days later it was ready and we could pick it up. Then we were actually registered. It was really easy and the staff at Student Affaird spoke english.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The student affairs office helped us alot. Our contact person was always ready to answer our emails as well.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: We needed to change some of our classes upon arrival. But we were succesful with those.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Always just ask if you are unsure of something. They are there to help and guide you. And dont worry, everything will be done it just always takes longer in Turkey.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was very high, language wise. I did not feel fully prepared for the classes. My level of Turkish was not good enough for the classes. But I got the feeling that the classes wasn't actually that difficult, if you know the language well.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was only classes where the teacher was talking from a powerpoint. And of course the students could ask questions, but it was never group work or anything. Just sit and listen (and take notes..)

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer: I would recommend Avrupa"da Türkce, I thought it was interesting.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I didn't have any unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: As every else in the world everything has gone up in price. So I wasn't shocked to find out that everything was getting more expensive, but Turkey is still a cheap country to live in.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They had a lot of "clubs" that you could be a part of. Sport, politics, arts and so on.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I dont know since I didn't participate in them.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Ankara does not have that much to offer "tourist" wise. There is a few things that you can see, and sure go see those. Otherwise I would recommend taking a weekend trip to another city fx Istanbul.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I thought it was very easy. You just have to get used to everything is being done slower. The bus? Never comes on time, or sometimes is doesnt even show up. Do you need someone to fix something in your apartment? They can come next week. But the turkish people are the most helpful people on the planet. They will help you with anything you need!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The local students didn't talk to us so no. I do not have any tips.. Our turkish was not good enough to communicate with them and their english was not good enough to communicate with us.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They are very helpful people

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Meet up with the other Erasmus students!! Go out, have fun, do something all the time (if you want). Don't stress.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be ready for classes and ACADEMIC turkish. It is going to be difficult, but hang in there.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I do feel like I have improved my language skills in Turkish.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language...

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
